incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: Canary rollout v5.2.0 -> v5.3.0 increased tail latency in eu-west-1. p95 220ms -> 1.4s, p99 480ms -> 2.8s. Streaming stalls observed. Paging Leah (oncall). Links: https://observability/reports/2187654321
Leah (oncall): Acked. I'm on it. Allocating paging channel. Any immediate customer impact known?
Aisha (support): I'm seeing 3 customer tickets in EU complaining about timeouts for streaming sessions in the last 4m. Tix #987, #988, #989. Customers report partial responses then hang.
Marco (eng-runtime): Confirmed. Canary fleet (model:gpt-redwood-compat, variant:q4) rolled to 20% last deploy at 2187654200. Metrics show concurrent streaming stream_open succeed but stall during token emission: spikes in async write latency to gRPC workers. Kernel-level latencies up on GPU node group rg-eu-enc-3.
Leah (oncall): What's the easiest mitigation? Can we cut canary back to 0% while we investigate?
Marco (eng-runtime): Yes — recommend immediate rollback of traffic split to previous model and enable fallback route to stable cache-enabled variant.
Priya (eng-sre): I can run the rollback. Command to shift traffic:
```
# infractl traffic set-split --service=canary-model --to=stable --percent=100 --region=eu-west-1
```
Executing now.
CLI-deploy-bot: started job 6721: `traffic set-split` (eu-west-1) — ETA ~30s
Marco (eng-runtime): Also toggling streaming backpressure setting to strict to avoid head-of-line stalls: `STREAMING_BACKPRESSURE=enabled` on canary router. Doing a safe toggle (no restart) applied to 4/5 routers.
Leah (oncall): Priya, confirm rollback success and whether p99 returns to baseline. Aisha, please notify affected customers we're rolling back and will follow up.
Priya (eng-sre): rollback done — job 6721 completed. New split = stable:100 canary:0. Verifying metrics.
Marco (eng-runtime): Seeing immediate improvement in request latency on proxy: p95 down from 1.4s to 250ms within 60s. p99 trending to ~420ms. Streaming stalls reduced — outstanding stalled streams decreased from 120 -> 6.
Aisha (support): Messaging customers now: "We've rolled back a canary variant in EU and are monitoring. We'll follow up with root cause and ETA for a safe re-rollout." :speech_balloon: 
Daniel (prod): Thanks team. Was the issue model-level (q4 quant) or infra (kernel selection)? Marco, what telemetry points to root cause?
Marco (eng-runtime): Early signals: increased kernel launch latency correlated with specific token types (Unicode category) and longer attention windows in v5.3 change. Also our async writer queue length spiked when sequence lengths >512. Hypothesis: new fused-kernel path has a bug that stalls token emission under steady batching of long sequences.
Priya (eng-sre): Node rg-eu-enc-3 had CPU steal spikes during the rollout window — investigating whether scheduling + kernel path combo exacerbated the stalls.
Leah (oncall): For now: 1) incident severity - P2 (widespread customer impact but mitigated by rollback), 2) keep oncall until postmortem kickoff, 3) schedule immediate canary freeze until root cause fixed.
Marco (eng-runtime): I'll open a bug and attach traces and perf profiles. Assigning to runtime-team for blocker fix. Repro steps in lab: replay traffic with long sequences and fused-kernel enabled.
Priya (eng-sre): Adding follow-up tasks: diag GPU kernels, audit recent kernel selector changes, check libcu updates. Capturing node snapshots.
Leah (oncall): Handing off monitoring and remediation to Marco/Priya for live mitigation. I'll create an incident ticket and start the postmortem doc. Aisha, please send CS follow-up with expected timeline (2-4 hours for initial RCA).
Aisha (support): Will do. Draft message posted to #customers-eu and will update the 3 tickets. :white_check_mark:
Marco (eng-runtime): Quick note — if rollback didn't cut it, plan B is to route EU traffic to us-west-1 via emergency routing and enable KV-prefix caching for common prompts.
Leah (oncall): Noted. Closing paging for now. If metrics regress reopen. Thanks all — good job fast rollback. :thumbsup:
